vsm2.12:93.2: “He is normally an obtainer of the water-kasiṇa attainment.
vsm2.12:93.4: Having adverted, he resolves with knowledge: “Let there be water.”
vsm2.12:93.6: He does the diving in and out of the earth.
vsm2.12:93.7: Just as men normally not possessed of supernormal power do diving in and out of water,
vsm2.12:93.8:
so this possessor of supernormal power, by his attaining mental mastery,
does the diving in and out of the earth as though in water” (Paṭis II 208).
vsm2.12:94.1:
And he does not only dive in and out, but whatever else he wants, such as bathing,
drinking, mouth washing, washing of chattels, and so on.
vsm2.12:94.2: And not only water, but there is whatever else (liquid that) he wants, such as ghee, oil, honey, molasses, and so on.
vsm2.12:94.3:
When he does the preliminary work, after adverting thus, “Let there be so
much of this and this” and resolves, it becomes as he resolved.
vsm2.12:94.4: If he takes them and fills dishes with them, the ghee is only ghee, the oil, etc., only oil, etc., the water only water.
vsm2.12:94.5: If he wants to be wetted by it, he is wetted, if he does not want to be wetted by it, he is not wetted.
vsm2.12:94.6: And it is only for him that that earth becomes water, not for anyone else.
vsm2.12:94.7: People go on it on foot and in vehicles, etc., and they do their ploughing, etc., there.
vsm2.12:94.8: But if he wishes, “Let it be water for them too,” it becomes water for them too.
vsm2.12:94.9:
When the time determined has elapsed, all the extent determined, except for water
originally present in water pots, ponds, etc., becomes earth again.
vsm2.12:95.2: here water that one sinks into when trodden on is called “broken,”
vsm2.12:95.4: But one who wants to go in this way should attain the earth-kasiṇa jhāna and emerge.
vsm2.12:95.5:
Then he should do the preliminary work, determining thus, “Let the water in such an area
become earth,” and he should resolve in the way already described.
vsm2.12:95.6: Simultaneously with the resolve, the water in that place becomes earth.
vsm2.12:96.2: “He is normally an obtainer of the earth-kasiṇa attainment.
vsm2.12:96.4: Having adverted, he resolves with knowledge: ‘Let there be earth.’
vsm2.12:96.7: Just as men normally not possessed of supernormal power go on unbroken earth,
vsm2.12:96.8: so this possessor of supernormal power, by his attaining of mental mastery, goes on unbroken water as if on earth” (Paṭis II 208).
vsm2.12:97.1: And he not only goes, but he adopts whatever posture he wishes.
vsm2.12:97.2: And not only earth, but whatever else solid that he wants such as gems, gold, rocks, trees, etc.
vsm2.12:97.3: he adverts to that and resolves, and it becomes as he resolves.
vsm2.12:97.4: And that water becomes earth only for him; it is water for anyone else.
vsm2.12:97.5: And fishes and turtles and water birds go about there as they like.
vsm2.12:97.6: But if he wishes to make it earth for other people, he does so too.
vsm2.12:97.7: When the time determined has elapsed, it becomes water again.
vsm2.12:98.1: Seated cross-legged he travels: he goes seated cross-legged.
vsm2.12:98.2: Like a winged bird: like a bird furnished with wings.
vsm2.12:98.3: One who wants to do this should attain the earth kasiṇa and emerge.
vsm2.12:98.4:
Then if he wants to go cross-legged, he should do the preliminary work and determine an area
the size of a seat for sitting cross-legged on, and he should resolve in the way already described.
vsm2.12:98.5: If he wants to go lying down, he determines an area the size of a bed.
vsm2.12:98.6:
If he wants to go on foot, he determines a suitable area the size of a path, and he
resolves in the way already described: “Let it be earth.”
vsm2.12:98.7: Simultaneously with the resolve it becomes earth.
vsm2.12:99.2: “‘Seated cross-legged he travels in space like a winged bird’:
vsm2.12:99.3: he is normally an obtainer of the earth-kasiṇa attainment. He adverts to space.
vsm2.12:99.4: Having adverted, he resolves with knowledge: ‘Let there be earth.’
vsm2.12:99.6: He travels (walks), stands, sits, and lies down in space, in the sky.
vsm2.12:99.7: Just as men normally not possessed of supernormal power travel (walk), stand, sit, and lie down on earth,
vsm2.12:99.8:
so this possessor of supernormal power, by his attaining of mental mastery, travels (walks),
stands, sits, and lies down in space, in the sky” (Paṭis II 208).
vsm2.12:100.1: And a bhikkhu who wants to travel in space should be an obtainer of the divine eye.
vsm2.12:100.3:
On the way there may be mountains, trees, etc., that are temperature-originated, or jealous nāgas,
supaṇṇas, etc., may create them. He will need to be able to see these.
vsm2.12:100.4: But what should be done on seeing them?
vsm2.12:100.5: He should attain the basic jhāna and emerge, and then he should do the preliminary work thus, “Let there be space,” and resolve.
vsm2.12:101.1: But the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷa-Abhaya said:
vsm2.12:101.2: “Friends, what is the use of attaining the attainment? Is not his mind concentrated?
vsm2.12:101.3: Hence any area that he has resolved thus, ‘Let it be space’ is space.”
vsm2.12:101.4: Though he spoke thus, nevertheless the matter should be treated as described under the miracle of going unhindered through walls.
vsm2.12:101.5:
Moreover, he should be an obtainer of the divine eye for the purpose of descending in a secluded
place, for if he descends in a public place, in a bathing place, or at a village gate,
vsm2.12:101.6: he is exposed to the multitude.
vsm2.12:101.7: So, seeing with the divine eye, he should avoid a place where there is no open space and descend in an open space.
vsm2.12:102.1: With his hand he touches and strokes the moon and sun so mighty and powerful:
vsm2.12:102.2:
here the “might” of the moon and sun should be understood to consist in the fact
that they travel at an altitude of forty-two thousand leagues,
vsm2.12:102.3: and their “power” to consist in their simultaneous illuminating of three of the four continents.
vsm2.12:102.4: Or they are “mighty” because they travel overhead and give light as they do, and they are “powerful” because of that same might.
vsm2.12:102.5: He touches: he seizes, or he touches in one place.
vsm2.12:102.6: Strokes: he strokes all over, as if it were the surface of a looking-glass.
vsm2.12:103.1:
This supernormal power is successful simply through the jhāna that is made
the basis for direct-knowledge; there is no special kasiṇa attainment here.
vsm2.12:103.2: For this is said in the Paṭisambhidā:
vsm2.12:103.3:
“‘With his hand … so mighty and powerful’: here this possessor of supernormal power
who has attained mind mastery … adverts to the moon and sun.
vsm2.12:103.4: Having adverted, he resolves with knowledge: ‘Let it be within hand’s reach.’
vsm2.12:103.6: Sitting or lying down, with his hand he touches, makes contact with, strokes the moon and sun.
vsm2.12:103.7: Just as men normally not possessed of supernormal power touch, make contact with, stroke, some material object within hand’s reach,
vsm2.12:103.8:
so this possessor of supernormal power, by his attaining of mental mastery, sitting or lying
down, with his hands touches, makes contact with, strokes the moon and sun” (Paṭis II 298).
vsm2.12:104.1: If he wants to go and touch them, he goes and touches them.
vsm2.12:104.2: But if he wants to touch them here sitting or lying down, he resolves: “Let them be within hand’s reach.”
vsm2.12:104.3:
Then he either touches them as they stand within hand’s reach when they have come by the power of the resolve
like palmyra fruits loosened from their stalk, or he does so by enlarging his hand.
vsm2.12:104.4: But when he enlarges his hand, does he enlarge what is clung to or what is not clung to?
vsm2.12:104.5: He enlarges what is not clung to supported by what is clung to.
vsm2.12:105.1: Here the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷa-Nāga said:
vsm2.12:105.2: “But, friends, why does what is clung to not become small and big too?
vsm2.12:105.3: When a bhikkhu comes out through a keyhole, does not what is clung to become small?
vsm2.12:105.4: And when he makes his body big, does it not then become big, as in the case of the Elder Mahā Moggallāna?”
vsm2.12:106.1: At one time, it seems, when the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had heard the Blessed One preaching the Dhamma,
vsm2.12:106.2: he invited him thus, “Venerable sir, take alms at our house together with five hundred bhikkhus,” and then he departed.
vsm2.12:106.3:
The Blessed One consented. When the rest of that day and part of the night had passed,
he surveyed the ten-thousandfold world element in the early morning.
vsm2.12:106.4: Then the royal nāga (serpent) called Nandopananda came within the range of his knowledge.
vsm2.12:107.1:
The Blessed One considered him thus: “This royal nāga has come into the range of my knowledge.
Has he the potentiality for development?”
vsm2.12:107.2: Then he saw that he had wrong view and no confidence in the Three Jewels.
vsm2.12:107.3: He considered thus, “Who is there that can cure him of his wrong view?”
vsm2.12:107.4: He saw that the Elder Mahā Moggallāna could.
vsm2.12:107.5: Then when the night had turned to dawn, after he had seen to the needs of the body, he addressed the venerable Ānanda:
vsm2.12:107.6: “Ānanda, tell five hundred bhikkhus that the Perfect One is going on a visit to the gods.”
vsm2.12:108.1: It was on that day that they had got a banqueting place ready for Nandopananda.
vsm2.12:108.2:
He was sitting on a divine couch with a divine white parasol held aloft,
surrounded by the three kinds of dancers and a retinue of nāgas,
vsm2.12:108.3: and surveying the various kinds of food and drink served up in divine vessels.
vsm2.12:108.4:
Then the Blessed One so acted that the royal nāga saw him as he proceeded directly above
his canopy in the direction of the divine world of the Thirty-three, accompanied by the five hundred bhikkhus.
vsm2.12:109.1: Then this evil view arose in Nandopananda the royal nāga:
vsm2.12:109.2: “There go these bald-headed monks in and out of the realm of the Thirty-three directly over my realm.
vsm2.12:109.3: I will not have them scattering the dirt off their feet on our heads.”
vsm2.12:109.4: He got up, and he went to the foot of Sineru. Changing his form,
vsm2.12:109.5: he surrounded it seven times with his coils.
vsm2.12:109.6: Then he spread his hood over the realm of the Thirty-three and made everything there invisible.
vsm2.12:110.1: The venerable Raṭṭhapāla said to the Blessed One:
vsm2.12:110.2: “Venerable sir, standing in this place formerly I used to see Sineru and the ramparts of Sineru,
vsm2.12:110.3: and the Thirty-three, and the Vejayanta Palace, and the flag over the Vejayanta Palace.
vsm2.12:110.4: Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why I now see neither Sineru nor … the flag over the Vejayanta Palace?”
vsm2.12:110.5:
—“This royal nāga called Nandopananda is angry with us, Raṭṭhapāla. He has surrounded Sineru seven
times with his coils, and he stands there covering us with his raised hood, making it dark.”
vsm2.12:110.7: But the Blessed One would not allow it.
vsm2.12:110.8: Then the venerable Bhaddiya and the venerable Rāhula and all the bhikkhus in turn offered to do so,
vsm2.12:110.9: but the Blessed One would not allow it.
vsm2.12:111.1: Last of all the venerable Mahā Moggallāna said, “I will tame him, venerable sir.”
vsm2.12:111.2: The Blessed One allowed it, saying, “Tame him, Moggallāna.”
vsm2.12:111.3: The elder abandoned that form and assumed the form of a huge royal nāga,
vsm2.12:111.4:
and he surrounded Nandopananda fourteen times with his coils and raised his hood
above the other’s hood, and he squeezed him against Sineru.
vsm2.12:111.6: The elder said, “There is smoke not only in your body but also in mine,” and he produced smoke.
vsm2.12:111.7: The royal nāga’s smoke did not distress the elder, but the elder’s smoke distressed the royal nāga.
vsm2.12:111.8: Then the royal nāga produced flames.
vsm2.12:111.9: The elder said, “There is fire not only in your body but also in mine,” and he produced flames.
vsm2.12:111.10: The royal nāga’s fire did not distress the elder, but the elder’s fire distressed the royal nāga.
vsm2.12:112.1: The royal nāga thought, “He has squeezed me against Sineru, and he has produced both smoke and flames.”
vsm2.12:112.2: Then he asked, “Sir, who are you?”
vsm2.12:112.4: —“Venerable sir, resume your proper bhikkhu’s state.”
vsm2.12:112.5:
The elder abandoned that form, and he went into his right ear and came out from his left ear;
then he went into his left ear and came out from his right ear.
vsm2.12:112.6:
Likewise he went into his right nostril and came out from his left nostril;
then he went into his left nostril and came out from his right nostril.
vsm2.12:112.7: Then the royal nāga opened his mouth.
vsm2.12:112.8: The elder went inside it, and he walked up and down, east and west, inside his belly.
vsm2.12:113.1: The Blessed One said, “Moggallāna, Moggallāna, beware; this is a mighty nāga.”
vsm2.12:113.2:
The elder said, “Venerable sir, the four roads to power have been developed by me, repeatedly practiced,
made the vehicle, made the basis, established, consolidated, and properly undertaken.
vsm2.12:113.3: I can tame not only Nandopananda, venerable sir, but a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand royal nāgas like Nandopananda.”
vsm2.12:114.1:
The royal nāga thought, “When he went in the first place I did not see him. But now when
he comes out I shall catch him between my fangs and chew him up.”
vsm2.12:114.2: Then he said, “Venerable sir, come out. Do not keep troubling me by walking up and down inside my belly.”
vsm2.12:114.3: The elder came out and stood outside.
vsm2.12:114.4: The royal nāga recognized him, and blew a blast from his nose.
vsm2.12:114.5: The elder attained the fourth jhāna, and the blast failed to move even a single hair on his body.
vsm2.12:114.6:
The other bhikkhus would, it seems, have been able to perform all the miracles up to now, but at this point they could
not have attained with so rapid a response, which is why the Blessed One would not allow them to tame the royal nāga.
vsm2.12:115.1:
The royal nāga thought, “I have been unable to move even a single hair on this monk’s
body with the blast from my nose. He is a mighty monk.”
vsm2.12:115.2:
The elder abandoned that form, and having assumed the form of a supaṇṇa,
he pursued the royal nāga demonstrating the supaṇṇa’s blast.
vsm2.12:115.3:
The royal nāga abandoned that form, and having assumed the form of a young brahman, he said,
“Venerable sir, I go for refuge to you,” and he paid homage at the elder’s feet.
vsm2.12:115.4:
The elder said, “The Master has come, Nanda; come, let us go to him.” So having tamed the royal
nāga and deprived him of his poison, he went with him to the Blessed One’s presence.
vsm2.12:116.1: The royal nāga paid homage to the Blessed One and said, “Venerable sir, I go for refuge to you.”
vsm2.12:116.2: The Blessed One said, “May you be happy, royal nāga.” Then he went, followed by the Community of Bhikkhus, to Anāthapiṇḍika’s house.
vsm2.12:116.3: Anāthapiṇḍika said, “Venerable sir, why have you come so late?”
vsm2.12:116.4: —“There was a battle between Moggallāna and Nandopananda.”
vsm2.12:116.5: —“Who won, venerable sir? Who was defeated?”
vsm2.12:116.7:
Anāthapiṇḍika said, “Venerable sir, let the Blessed One consent to my providing meals for seven
days in a single series, and to my honouring the elder for seven days.”
vsm2.12:116.8: Then for seven days he accorded great honour to the five hundred bhikkhus with the Enlightened One at their head.
vsm2.12:117.1: So it was with reference to this enlarged form created during this taming of Nandopananda that it was said:
vsm2.12:117.2: “When he makes his body big, does it not then become big, as in the case of the Elder Mahā Moggallāna?” (§105).
vsm2.12:117.3: Although this was said, the bhikkhus observed, “He enlarges only what is not clung to supported by what is clung to.”
vsm2.12:117.4: And only this is correct here.
